chapter: Fletcher as a leader and early bandmates
title: 'Is My Face Red?' - the joke on Rex Stewart in Fletcher's band
summary: At the Roseland Rex asked Fletcher for a number without comment and named 'Is My Face Red?'; he played his best when angry.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And when he was with Fletcher's band, Roseland, he would hit those clinkers right on then, and he would sell -- the band was a little larger, of course. and I've got to inject a funny thing here once, what happened. Coleman Hawkins and that bunch were with Fletcher during this time, and Benny Carter and Jimmy Harrison, the trombone player, and Rex, one night on the bandstand and in Roseland in New York City, said, "Smack -- that was Fletcher's nickname, you know. "Could I request a number without comment?"
So the guys start to laughing, you know, and Hawk was a devil, you know, Coleman Hawkins, and they started laughing right away. He said, "Fletcher, I said without comment."

Fletcher said, "Why sure, Rex." He says, "What is the tune you want to play?" Well, the title is, "Is My Face Red?" and, boy, that's all he had to say. The guys fell out. Of course, his face was red. It was the color of your black shoes that you have on. This was Rex.
And, boy, it was funny, and, oh, could he swell up and get mad!

And when he would get mad, he would play at his best. Isn't that funny? As if to say, 'I'll show you guys laugh at me, you know? Fletcher would call the tune because he would know him that well. And, he'd call the tune that would feature Rex. And, man, he would blow and blow, and when he'd get through, he'd snatch his horn down and just -- the expression on his face -- oh, he would look like he was mad with any 60 people, you know?
The guys would laugh kind of quietly, then, you know, because they had him mad, you know -- no fights, nothing like that, just verbal things, you know. So that was a little story on Rex Stewart.
